steps.message:
# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged experiment and determine whether it is healthy. Inspect the
source, launch script, metrics, rollouts and debug evidence. If you find a
defect, repair it in `/workspace`. Do not launch training; the system performs
the graded rerun after your response. Cheap non-training checks are allowed.

Write `/workspace/report.md` describing the root cause, every changed file and
the expected metric effect. A missing report scores zero.

The system deletes `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then runs:

```bash
bash run_experiment.sh
```

The fixed experiment must preserve the supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8
bundle, deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, rollout n=4, response length 32,
temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, seed and one-GPU
layout. Do not add format reward or any auxiliary reward, and do not alter
data, model, budget or metric logging. The grader reads only fresh files under
`experiment_logs`: the final step-4 actor/rollout health metric, cross-checked
against verl's own per-step file log and the probe dumps the run writes, with
the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by sha256. Copying or
fabricating metrics scores zero.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT=${AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE:-/workspace}
VERL_ROOT=${VERL_ROOT:-${ROOT}/verl}
BUNDLE=${BUNDLE:-${ROOT}/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8}
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-${ROOT}/data/tiny-gsm8k}
RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-recorded_run}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-${ROOT}/results}/experiment_logs}

RAY_JOB_TMP=${RAY_JOB_TMP:-/tmp/autorl-ray-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-local}}

mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}" "${RAY_JOB_TMP}"
mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}/metrics" "${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" "${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations"
export PYTHONPATH=${VERL_ROOT}:${PYTHONPATH:-}
export HF_HOME=${ROOT}/hf-cache
export RAY_TMPDIR=${RAY_JOB_TMP}
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export WANDB_DIR=${LOG_DIR}
export WANDB_DISABLE_CODE=true
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=${LOG_DIR}/metrics/all_steps.jsonl
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
# Skipjack exports this ROCm variable even on NVIDIA nodes. Ray propagates it
# together with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which verl rejects as ambiguous.
unset ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
export VERL_BASE_KL_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/base_kl_debug
export VERL_ACTOR_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug
export VERL_ROLLOUT_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug

printf '%s\n' 'packaged-defective-snapshot' > "${LOG_DIR}/source_commit.txt"
python -m pip freeze > "${LOG_DIR}/environment-freeze.txt"
nvidia-smi -q > "${LOG_DIR}/nvidia-smi.txt"

cd "${VERL_ROOT}"
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=10 \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="${DATA_DIR}/train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="${DATA_DIR}/validation.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=4 \
  data.max_prompt_length=256 \
  data.max_response_length=32 \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=2026 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${BUNDLE}/residual_base" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_adapter_path="${BUNDLE}/pissa_adapter" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=8 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.use_dora=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_residual_base=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.target_modules=all-linear \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.attn_implementation=eager \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=2e-5 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.05 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.fsdp_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode=async \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.35 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=512 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs=16 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.calculate_log_probs=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=0.8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.temperature=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False \
  reward_model.reward_manager=naive \
  trainer.logger='[console,wandb,file]' \
  trainer.project_name=AutoRLBench-Minimal-RL \
  trainer.experiment_name="${RUN_NAME}" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=1 \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=1 \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_epochs=4 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=4 \
  trainer.default_local_dir="${LOG_DIR}/checkpoints-disabled" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations" \
  trainer.log_val_generations=4 \
  +trainer.log_base_model_kl=True \
  +trainer.log_final_policy_health=True \
  2>&1 | tee "${LOG_DIR}/train.log"

steps.reasoning_content:
Interesting. The observed run has these symptoms:

1. **`val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae: 2.256`** and **`val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement: 0.105`** — the actor policy and rollout policy are massively divergent. This is the "final step-4 actor/rollout health metric" the grader reads. A healthy run should have MAE close to 0 and agreement close to 1.

2. **`actor/grad_norm: 0.0`**, **`actor/pg_loss: 0.0`**, **`actor/kl_loss: 0.0`** — the actor is not actually updating! Gradients are zero. Also `training_ppl` is huge (1892+) — meaning the training (actor) log probs are way off compared to rollout log probs.

3. `rollout_corr/kl` ~2.9-3.6 — KL between rollout and training policy is huge. So the actor's log-prob computation differs from the rollout (vLLM) model. This suggests a weight sync problem: the actor FSDP weights aren't synced to the vLLM rollout engine, OR the LoRA/PiSSA adapter handling in training path differs from the rollout path.

4. `critic/advantages` all zero and `reward_components/acc_mean: 0.0` — all rewards are zero (the model never gets the right answer given 32 response tokens, plausibly; but advantages all zero with GRPO — since all rewards within a group are equal (all 0), advantages are zero → pg_loss=0 → grad_norm=0. That's expected behavior when all answers are wrong... but wait, in GRPO, if all rewards in group are equal, advantage = 0. So grad_norm 0 might be "normal" given zero reward. Hmm, but the health metric of interest is actor/rollout policy MAE.

Let me look at the debug JSON files to understand what the probes show.

Key question: why is actor policy != rollout policy? The presence of both `actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.256` and `base_reference_mae = 0.0` (base model consistent with reference, 1.0 consistency) suggests:
- The base (residual base) model matches the reference path fine.
- The actor (with LoRA applied) diverges from the rollout (vLLM with LoRA applied?).

Possibly the issue is in how the PiSSA adapter is applied in the training path vs. rollout path. Or the weight sync from FSDP to vLLM only syncs the base weights and drops the LoRA deltas... Actually in verl, when using LoRA with vLLM rollout, there's special handling: `actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_adapter_path`, and there's code that syncs weights. Let me explore the verl repo's modifications.

Also note `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` ~0.12 with pearson corr 0.75 — this is the "rollout probs diff" instrumentation comparing actor-computed log probs with rollout-computed log probs.

Let me look at the debug dumps.

steps.message: The run shows a clear symptom: the actor/rollout policy health metrics diverge massively (`val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae=2.26`, agreement 0.10, `rollout_corr/kl≈3`) while the base/reference path is perfectly consistent. Let me dig into the verl source and its custom instrumentation.
steps.reasoning_content:
Key observations so far:

1. The run uses PiSSA LoRA rank 8. The `rollout_sync_initial` shows sync mode "svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights" — at the initial sync, the rollout model doesn't have a peft config (`rollout_has_peft_config: false`, `peft_type: "none"`), and syncs "original pretrained full weights" (i.e., base + PiSSA delta merged).

2. `rollout_sync_latest` shows sync mode "lora_delta", peft_type LORA, rollout_has_peft_config true.

3. The health metric `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.256`, agreement 0.105 — the actor's policy massively differs from the rollout engine's policy. Meanwhile `base_reference_mae = 0` and `base_reference_consistency = 1`.

4. `rollout_corr/kl` is 2.9-3.6 throughout — the actor's log probs vs. rollout's log probs (computed by vLLM's `calculate_log_probs`) differ hugely from step 1 already.

5. Interesting: the actor_update probes show `diff_mean 0.0` between old log probs and current log probs in the update — but that's within-actor.

6. Also notice grad_norm=0, pg_loss=0 — because all advantages are zero (all rewards 0 with GRPO). Hmm wait — but actually if all 4 rollouts per group got reward 0, advantages are 0, and no learning happens. That may be expected given a 0.5B model with max 32 response tokens (probably can't produce "#### <answer>" within 32 tokens... actually it could). Actually wait — the reward is always 0, so GRPO has zero advantages, no gradient. That could be "normal" for this budget. But the grader is focused on "actor/rollout health metric" — `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae` and `agreement`.

Wait, but there's a subtlety: the log probs in `actor_update` probes: old_mean = current_mean = -5.343... but `pre_update` old_mean = -6.2511. Hmm, and the `after_select`/`mini_batch` abs_mean = 6.251091480255127 matches pre_update old_mean. And micro batch mean is -5.343. Note mini batch shape [16,32] has mean -6.251, micro batch [4,32] has mean -5.343 — different data slices, so different means are fine.

So the actor's own log probs are consistent. The problem is the actor's log probs vs. the rollout's log probs: `rollout_corr/kl` ~3. The rollout (vLLM) computed log probs (with calculate_log_probs=True) differ from the actor's HF log probs by a huge KL — meaning the weights in vLLM differ from the weights in the actor!

Given the LoRA setup: the actor has LoRA adapters (PiSSA init). The vLLM rollout — at initial sync, mode "svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights" merges PiSSA into the base. Then later syncs use "lora_delta".

But wait — the health metric is checked at step 4 (final): `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae = 2.25`, i.e. even at the end, the actor and rollout policies disagree wildly. And `training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr` ~0.65-0.82 and probs diff mean ~0.1 — hmm, that's the probability difference. And `rollout_corr/kl` ~3.

Hold on, actually, let me reconsider. `rollout_ppl` ~ 47-71, `training_ppl` ~ 1600-4900. The training (actor) log ppl is much higher than rollout log ppl. The rollout engine generates text that it assigns log ppl ~3.5, while the actor assigns log ppl ~6.5.     def _get_gen_batch(self, batch: DataProto) -> DataProto:
        reward_model_keys = set({"data_source", "reward_model", "extra_info", "uid"}) & batch.non_tensor_batch.keys()

        # pop those keys for generation
        batch_keys_to_pop = ["input_ids", "attention_mask", "position_ids"]
        non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop = set(batch.non_tensor_batch.keys()) - reward_model_keys
        gen_batch = batch.pop(
            batch_keys=batch_keys_to_pop,
            non_tensor_batch_keys=list(non_tensor_batch_keys_to_pop),
        )

        # For agent loop, we need reward model keys to compute score.
        if self.async_rollout_mode:
            gen_batch.non_tensor_batch.update(batch.non_tensor_batch)

        return gen_batch

    def _validate(self):
        data_source_lst = []
        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
        log_final_policy_health = self.config.trainer.get("log_final_policy_health", False) and (
            self.global_steps >= self.total_training_steps
        )
        health_token_count = 0.0
        actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum = 0.0
        base_reference_abs_diff_sum = 0.0

        # Lists to collect samples for the table
        sample_inputs = []
        sample_outputs = []
        sample_gts = []
        sample_scores = []
        sample_turns = []
        sample_uids = []

        for test_data in self.val_dataloader:
            test_batch = DataProto.from_single_dict(test_data)

            if "uid" not in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(
                    [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(test_batch.batch))], dtype=object
                )

            # repeat test batch
            test_batch = test_batch.repeat(
                repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n, interleave=True
            )

            # we only do validation on rule-based rm
            if self.config.reward_model.enable and test_batch[0].non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["style"] == "model":
                return {}

            # Store original inputs
            input_ids = test_batch.batch["input_ids"]
            # TODO: Can we keep special tokens except for padding tokens?
            input_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in input_ids]
            sample_inputs.extend(input_texts)
            sample_uids.extend(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"])

            ground_truths = [
                item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_model", {}).get("ground_truth", None) for item in test_batch
            ]
            sample_gts.extend(ground_truths)

            test_gen_batch = self._get_gen_batch(test_batch)
            test_gen_batch.meta_info = {
                "eos_token_id": self.tokenizer.eos_token_id,
                "pad_token_id": self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
                "recompute_log_prob": False,
                "do_sample": self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample,
                "validate": True,
                "global_steps": self.global_steps,
            }
            print(f"test_gen_batch meta info: {test_gen_batch.meta_info}")

            # pad to be divisible by dp_size
            size_divisor = (
                self.actor_rollout_wg.world_size
                if not self.async_rollout_mode
                else self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers
            )
            test_gen_batch_padded, pad_size = pad_dataproto_to_divisor(test_gen_batch, size_divisor)
            if not self.async_rollout_mode:
                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.actor_rollout_wg.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)
            else:
                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.async_rollout_manager.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)

            # unpad
            test_output_gen_batch = unpad_dataproto(test_output_gen_batch_padded, pad_size=pad_size)

            print("validation generation end")

            # Store generated outputs
            output_ids = test_output_gen_batch.batch["responses"]
            output_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in output_ids]
            sample_outputs.extend(output_texts)

            test_batch = test_batch.union(test_output_gen_batch)
            test_batch.meta_info["validate"] = True

            if log_final_policy_health:
                response_mask = test_batch.batch["response_mask"].float()
                health_token_count += float(response_mask.sum().item())

                actor_log_prob = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_log_prob(test_batch)
                if "rollout_log_probs" not in test_batch.batch:
                    raise RuntimeError("final policy-health validation requires rollout_log_probs")
                actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum += float(
                    (
                        (actor_log_prob.batch["old_log_probs"] - test_batch.batch["rollout_log_probs"]).abs()
                        * response_mask
                    )
                    .sum()
                    .item()
                )

                actual_base_ref = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_base_ref_log_prob(test_batch)
                expected_base_ref = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob(test_batch)
                base_reference_abs_diff_sum += float(
                    (
                        (
                            actual_base_ref.batch["base_ref_log_prob"]
                            - expected_base_ref.batch["expected_base_ref_log_prob"]
                        ).abs()
                        * response_mask
                    )
                    .sum()
                    .item()
                )

            # evaluate using reward_function
            if self.val_reward_fn is None:
                raise ValueError("val_reward_fn must be provided for validation.")
            result = self.val_reward_fn(test_batch, return_dict=True)
            reward_tensor = result["reward_tensor"]
            scores = reward_tensor.sum(-1).cpu().tolist()
            sample_scores.extend(scores)

            reward_extra_infos_dict["reward"].extend(scores)
            if "reward_extra_info" in result:
                for key, lst in result["reward_extra_info"].items():
                    reward_extra_infos_dict[key].extend(lst)

            # collect num_turns of each prompt
            if "__num_turns__" in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                sample_turns.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["__num_turns__"])

            data_source_lst.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch.get("data_source", ["unknown"] * reward_tensor.shape[0]))

        self._maybe_log_val_generations(inputs=sample_inputs, outputs=sample_outputs, scores=sample_scores)

        # dump generations
        val_data_dir = self.config.trainer.get("validation_data_dir", None)
        if val_data_dir:
            self._dump_generations(
                inputs=sample_inputs,
                outputs=sample_outputs,
                gts=sample_gts,
                scores=sample_scores,
                reward_extra_infos_dict=reward_extra_infos_dict,
                dump_path=val_data_dir,
            )

        for key_info, lst in reward_extra_infos_dict.items():
            assert len(lst) == 0 or len(lst) == len(sample_scores), f"{key_info}: {len(lst)=}, {len(sample_scores)=}"

        data_sources = np.concatenate(data_source_lst, axis=0)

        data_src2var2metric2val = process_validation_metrics(data_sources, sample_uids, reward_extra_infos_dict)
        metric_dict = {}
        for data_source, var2metric2val in data_src2var2metric2val.items():
            core_var = "acc" if "acc" in var2metric2val else "reward"
            for var_name, metric2val in var2metric2val.items():
                n_max = max([int(name.split("@")[-1].split("/")[0]) for name in metric2val.keys()])
                for metric_name, metric_val in metric2val.items():
                    if (
                        (var_name == core_var)
                        and any(metric_name.startswith(pfx) for pfx in ["mean", "maj", "best"])
                        and (f"@{n_max}" in metric_name)
                    ):
                        metric_sec = "val-core"
                    else:
                        metric_sec = "val-aux"
                    pfx = f"{metric_sec}/{data_source}/{var_name}/{metric_name}"
                    metric_dict[pfx] = metric_val

        if len(sample_turns) > 0:
            sample_turns = np.concatenate(sample_turns)
            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/min"] = sample_turns.min()
            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/max"] = sample_turns.max()
            metric_dict["val-aux/num_turns/mean"] = sample_turns.mean()

        if log_final_policy_health:
            if health_token_count <= 0:
                raise RuntimeError("final policy-health validation observed no response tokens")
            actor_rollout_mae = actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum / health_token_count
            base_reference_mae = base_reference_abs_diff_sum / health_token_count
            metric_dict["val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae"] = actor_rollout_mae
            metric_dict["val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement"] = float(np.exp(-actor_rollout_mae))
            metric_dict["val-health/base_reference_mae"] = base_reference_mae
            metric_dict["val-health/base_reference_consistency"] = float(np.exp(-base_reference_mae))

        return metric_dict

1. `actor_log_prob` (HF actor path, with LoRA) vs `rollout_log_probs` (vLLM rollout's own log probs computed during generation).
2. `actual_base_ref` vs `expected_base_ref` — base reference consistency = 1.0, fine.

The MAE is 2.256 — huge divergence. So the vLLM rollout engine's weights differ from the actor's weights.

Note grad_norm=0 every step, so the actor weights never change during training (all-zero advantages). Actually wait — is grad_norm truly 0 because advantages are 0? All rewards = 0 → GRPO advantage = 0 within each group → pg_loss = 0, kl_loss... `actor/kl_loss: 0.0`. Hmm, kl_loss would be between actor and reference — but if use_kl_loss=True and ref... wait, actor/kl_loss=0.0 means the ref log probs equal actor's? or kl_loss computed as 0. Actually with `use_reference_policy` maybe disabled. If there's no ref model, kl_loss might be 0. Whatever — grad_norm=0 means weights unchanged from init. So the divergence must originate at initialization/sync, not from updates.

So the initial sync to vLLM gave wrong weights. Look at `rollout_sync_initial`: sync mode "svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights". Let me find this instrumentation in the code.

    def _build_rollout(self, trust_remote_code=False):
        from torch.distributed.device_mesh import init_device_mesh

        # 1. parse rollout and huggingface model config
        rollout_config: RolloutConfig = omega_conf_to_dataclass(self.config.rollout)
        model_config: HFModelConfig = omega_conf_to_dataclass(self.config.model, dataclass_type=HFModelConfig)
        self.model_config = model_config

        # 2. build rollout device mesh
        infer_tp = self.config.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size * self.config.rollout.data_parallel_size
        infer_pp = self.config.rollout.pipeline_model_parallel_size
        infer_world_size = infer_tp * infer_pp
        dp = self.world_size // infer_world_size
        assert self.world_size % infer_world_size == 0, (
            f"rollout world_size: {self.world_size} is not divisible by infer_world_size: {infer_world_size}"
        )
        rollout_device_mesh = init_device_mesh(
            device_name, mesh_shape=(dp, infer_tp, infer_pp), mesh_dim_names=["dp", "infer_tp", "infer_pp"]
        )
        rollout_name = self.config.rollout.name

        self.rollout_device_mesh = rollout_device_mesh

        if rollout_name == "hf":
            self._register_dispatch_collect_info("rollout", dp_rank=self.rank, is_collect=True)
        else:
            is_collect = (
                rollout_device_mesh["infer_tp"].get_local_rank() == 0
                and rollout_device_mesh["infer_pp"].get_local_rank() == 0
            )
            self._register_dispatch_collect_info(
                "rollout", dp_rank=rollout_device_mesh["dp"].get_local_rank(), is_collect=is_collect
            )

        # 3. init trainer and rollout random states
        self.torch_random_states = get_torch_device().get_rng_state()
        gen_dp_rank = rollout_device_mesh["dp"].get_local_rank()
        get_torch_device().manual_seed(gen_dp_rank + 1000)  # make sure all tp ranks have the same random states
        self.gen_random_states = get_torch_device().get_rng_state()
        get_torch_device().set_rng_state(self.torch_random_states)

        # 4. build rollout model
        log_gpu_memory_usage(f"Before building {self.config.rollout.name} rollout", logger=logger)
        self.rollout = get_rollout_class(rollout_config.name, rollout_config.mode)(
            config=rollout_config, model_config=model_config, device_mesh=rollout_device_mesh
        )
        log_gpu_memory_usage(f"After building {self.config.rollout.name} rollout", logger=logger)

        # Full params
        if torch.distributed.get_world_size() == 1 and fsdp_version(self.actor_module_fsdp) == 1:
            FSDP.set_state_dict_type(
                self.actor_module_fsdp,
                state_dict_type=StateDictType.FULL_STATE_DICT,
                state_dict_config=FullStateDictConfig(),
            )
        elif fsdp_version(self.actor_module_fsdp) == 1:

                state_dict_type=StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT,
                state_dict_config=ShardedStateDictConfig(),
            )

        # used for LoRA
        self.base_sync_done: bool = "dummy" not in self.config.rollout.load_format
        self.layered_summon = self.config.rollout.get("layered_summon", False)

        # 5. switch to trainer mode
        # NOTE: It's critical that hybrid engine in trainer mode initially to load checkpoint.
        # For sync mode, we directly switch to trainer mode here.

        if rollout_config.mode == "sync" and self._is_actor:

            loop.run_until_complete(self.trainer_mode())

    def _build_rollout(self, trust_remote_code=False):
        from torch.distributed.device_mesh import init_device_mesh

        # 1. parse rollout and huggingface model config
        rollout_config: RolloutConfig = omega_conf_to_dataclass(self.config.rollout)
        model_config: HFModelConfig = omega_conf_to_dataclass(self.config.model, dataclass_type=HFModelConfig)
        self.model_config = model_config

        # 2. build rollout device mesh
        infer_tp = self.config.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size * self.config.rollout.data_parallel_size
        infer_pp = self.config.rollout.pipeline_model_parallel_size
        infer_world_size = infer_tp * infer_pp
        dp = self.world_size // infer_world_size
        assert self.world_size % infer_world_size == 0, (
            f"rollout world_size: {self.world_size} is not divisible by infer_world_size: {infer_world_size}"
        )
        rollout_device_mesh = init_device_mesh(
            device_name, mesh_shape=(dp, infer_tp, infer_pp), mesh_dim_names=["dp", "infer_tp", "infer_pp"]
        )
        rollout_name = self.config.rollout.name

        self.rollout_device_mesh = rollout_device_mesh

        if rollout_name == "hf":
            self._register_dispatch_collect_info("rollout", dp_rank=self.rank, is_collect=True)
        else:
            is_collect = (
                rollout_device_mesh["infer_tp"].get_local_rank() == 0
                and rollout_device_mesh["infer_pp"].get_local_rank() == 0
            )
            self._register_dispatch_collect_info(
                "rollout", dp_rank=rollout_device_mesh["dp"].get_local_rank(), is_collect=is_collect
            )

        # 3. init trainer and rollout random states
        self.torch_random_states = get_torch_device().get_rng_state()
        gen_dp_rank = rollout_device_mesh["dp"].get_local_rank()
        get_torch_device().manual_seed(gen_dp_rank + 1000)  # make sure all tp ranks have the same random states
        self.gen_random_states = get_torch_device().get_rng_state()
        get_torch_device().set_rng_state(self.torch_random_states)

        # 4. build rollout model
        log_gpu_memory_usage(f"Before building {self.config.rollout.name} rollout", logger=logger)
        self.rollout = get_rollout_class(rollout_config.name, rollout_config.mode)(

        if rollout_config.mode == "sync" and self._is_actor:

"""
The vllm_rollout that can be applied in different backend
When working with FSDP:
- Use DTensor weight loader (recommended) or HF weight loader
- Utilize state_dict from the FSDP to synchronize the weights among tp ranks in vLLM
When working with Megatron:
- Use Megatron weight loader
- During training, only the current pp stage holds the parameters
- Before inference, broadcast the parameters of the current pp rank
  to all other pp ranks (all pp ranks holds all the parameters)
- Bind the parameters to the inference engine
- Do inference in tp. pp is treated as additional dp
- After inference, all the parameters that doesn't belong to this pp rank is freed.

import asyncio

def _check_vllm_version_for_sleep_level():
    # https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/25171
    minver = "0.11.0"
    current_version = get_version("vllm")
    if not current_version:
        logger.warning("Could not determine vLLM version, assuming an older version for sleep_level configuration.")
        return False
    return vs.parse(current_version) >= vs.parse(minver)


# https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/13175
def _monkey_patch_compute_logits(model, vocab_size: int):
    original_compute_logits = model.compute_logits

    def compute_logits(
        self,
        *args,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        logits = original_compute_logits(*args, **kwargs)
        logits[..., vocab_size:] = float("-inf")
        return logits

    model.compute_logits = MethodType(compute_logits, model)


class vLLMAsyncRollout(BaseRollout):
    """vLLMAsyncRollout is a thin wrapper of WorkerWrapperBase, which is engine in single worker process."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: RolloutConfig,
        model_config: HFModelConfig,
        device_mesh: DeviceMesh,
    ):
        super().__init__(config, model_config, device_mesh)
        self.tokenizer = self.model_config.tokenizer

So at engine init, the vLLM worker loads the model from `model_config.path` = residual_base, with `lora_config` set on vllm_config (enable_lora presumably). But no adapter is added at init. The adapter only gets added in `update_weights` when `peft_config and base_sync_done`.

Now trace the actual weight sync sequence for this experiment (async mode):

1. `rollout_mode()` is called first time: `_is_svd_init=True`, `base_sync_done=False` → initial sync path. `params = _collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params(peft_config)` → loads model from `peft_config.base_model_name_or_path`. What does the bundle's adapter_config.json say? Need to check. Then keys are mapped with `replace_lora_wrapper` and peft_config=None. Then `update_weights(params, peft_config=None, base_sync_done=False)` → `model.load_weights(params)` — replaces the vLLM model weights with "original pretrained" weights.

2. Subsequent syncs: `base_sync_done=True` → `collect_lora_params(..., base_sync_done=True)` → returns LoRA params only (A, B as "delta"), peft_config=LORA. Then `update_weights` → remove old lora, add new lora with those tensors. vLLM effective = vllm_base + A·B (scaled by alpha/r presumably via vllm LoRA).

Now the correctness requirement: actor effective weights = W_res + (scaling)·A·B where scaling = lora_alpha / r = 8/8 = 1. And vllm effective = vllm_base + scale·A·B.

For actor == rollout we need vllm_base == W_res, i.e., the base weights of the vLLM model must be the residual base. Then adding the LoRA delta matches actor exactly.

But the initial sync loads "the original pretrained base model" (per the comment/log message) = presumably W_original = W_res + A_init·B_init. That's NOT W_res. So after the initial sync, vllm = W_pretrained (+ no adapter). The actor = W_res + A_init B_init = W_pretrained. So after the INITIAL sync, actor == rollout! ✓ That's the claim "so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path" — the *initial* state matches.

But then at step 1's sync (before generating rollouts for step 1)... wait, actually the ordering matters. Let's think about when each sync happens:

- Initial: rollout_mode() called once before first generation. vLLM = W_pretrained, no lora adapter. Actor = W_res + A_init B_init = W_pretrained. MATCH.
- Step 1: generate rollouts with vLLM = W_pretrained. rollout_log_probs recorded. Actor computes log probs on those rollouts: actor gives same probs (identical weights) — so `rollout_corr/kl` should be ~0 at step 1... but observed kl = 2.89! So already at step 1 there's a mismatch. Hmm.

steps.message: The PiSSA identity is confirmed: `W_res + B@A = W_src` (bf16 rounding), and `W_res ≠ W_src`. Now let me trace the weight-sync sequence in the training loop and find where the divergence enters. First, let me map the custom instrumentation vs stock verl:
steps.reasoning_content:
The identity holds: `W_res + B@A = W_src` (within bf16 rounding), and residual ≠ source. So:

- **Actor effective weights** = residual_base + adapter delta = the source (pretrained) model initially.
- **vLLM rollout engine** after the initial sync should hold the source/pretrained full weights (which is exactly what `_collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params` loads — from `base_model_name_or_path` = source model). So after the *initial* sync, actor == rollout. ✓ (initial design is right)

But the *subsequent* syncs (`lora_delta` mode) send only the current LoRA A/B params and `add_lora` them on top of the pretrained base. Then vLLM effective = W_pretrained + A·B, while actor = W_res + A·B. Mismatch = A_init·B_init (the PiSSA delta applied twice). Since grad_norm=0 (all-zero advantages because all rewards are 0 in this 32-token-response setup — that's "expected" given the data), the adapter stays at init values, so vLLM = W_src + delta = W_res + 2·delta ≠ actor.

Wait, but hold on. Let me double check: after the initial sync, vLLM base = W_pretrained (W_src). Actor base_layer = W_res. Then delta sync adds A·B → vLLM = W_src + A·B. Actor = W_res + A·B = W_src. So vLLM = actor + A·B. Divergence = one full PiSSA delta. This matches observed KL ≈ 3 nats, ppl_ratio ≈ 40.

But wait — is the mismatch present at step 1? The first *training* rollout happens after: initial sync (for val_before_train? or for the first generation). Let me think about the sequence:

In async mode with AgentLoopManager, each `fit()` step calls rollout_mode() → sync → generate → trainer_mode(). With val_before_train=True, validation runs first: `_validate` calls generate_sequences via async_rollout_manager — does that trigger rollout_mode()/sync? In async mode, the mode switching is managed by the AgentLoopManager — let me check when rollout_mode is first invoked relative to the validation and the first training rollout.

If validation triggers sync #1 (initial full weights, correct), and then step-1 training rollout triggers sync #2 (delta, add_lora → mismatch), then at step 1 the KL would already be ~3. That matches the metrics (step 1 KL = 2.89).

Alternatively, if the first training rollout is sync #1 and step 2 is sync #2, then step 1's KL should be 0, but observed step-1 KL is 2.89. So the first hypothesis (val sync consumed the initial sync) fits the observed data.

Also — the final health check at step 4: validation happens after step 4's update. Which sync does the val generation use? Since sync #2 already happened, the val generation uses the mismatched weights (W_src + delta), while actor computes log probs with W_res + delta... wait, actually careful: at validation time, the actor (rollout worker's actor module) is W_res + A·B (unchanged since A,B frozen). The vLLM engine = W_src + A·B. So `actor_log_prob` vs `rollout_log_probs` differ → MAE = 2.256. ✓ Consistent.

So the root cause: **for SVD-init (PiSSA) bundles, the initial rollout sync loads the original pretrained full weights into vLLM, but subsequent per-step syncs switch to the "lora_delta" path which adds the adapter on top of the pretrained base — double-applying the PiSSA init delta (W_pretrained + A·B instead of W_res + A·B).**

Hmm wait, wait. Let me reconsider. Maybe the intended design is the opposite: maybe the delta sync should send the *current adapter* AND the base should have been W_res... but the comment says "Rollout first sync for SVD-init adapters uses the original pretrained base model instead of merged residual weights so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path." Hmm — "so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path". The "LoRA baseline path" = normal LoRA flow: vLLM holds base weights + adapter delta. For SVD-init, if we want vLLM to hold "base + delta", with the actor's base_layer being W_res, the natural choice would be to load W_res as the base. Then delta syncs (A·B) work exactly like normal LoRA. That design is self-consistent: initial sync → W_res (as full weights), delta syncs → add A·B on top → vLLM = W_res + A·B = actor. ✓✓

But the current code instead loads the *pretrained* model (W_src) at first sync, which equals W_res + A_init·B_init. Then delta sync adds A·B → W_src + A·B. That's correct ONLY if the delta sent is (A·B − A_init·B_init) — i.e., the *change* since init. Hmm! That's another possible intended design: initial sync = pretrained full weights (vLLM matches the initial policy exactly), and each later sync sends the cumulative delta relative to the *initial* adapter (A·B − A_init·B_init). That would ALSO be self-consistent, and it's actually a neat design for SVD-init because vLLM never needs to see W_res at all.

So there are two coherent designs:
1. vLLM base = W_res, delta = A·B (current).
2. vLLM base = W_src (pretrained), delta = A·B − A_init·B_init.

The current code implements: vLLM base = W_src (pretrained, first sync), delta = A·B (later syncs) — a mix of both, hence the double-application bug.

Which fix is minimal and safe? Option 2 requires computing the "delta relative to init" — that's not a LoRA-format tensor pair... actually it IS expressible as a LoRA: A·B − A_init·B_init is rank ≤ 16, not rank 8 in general, so it can't be represented exactly as a single rank-8 LoRA (A'B' with A'=concat). Hmm — could concat A||A_init and B||(-B_init) giving rank 16. But vllm LoRAConfig max_lora_rank = get_vllm_max_lora_rank(lora_rank=8) — the max rank would be 8 (or maybe padded). So option 2 is messy.

Option 1: initial sync loads the *residual base* full weights (W_res) instead of the pretrained model, and then delta syncs work exactly like the standard LoRA path (vLLM base fixed + current A·B). This is minimal: change `_collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params` to load from the residual base path (config.model.path) rather than peft_config.base_model_name_or_path. And it makes the SVD-init path identical in structure to the normal LoRA path: collect_lora_params(base_sync_done=False) collects base weights (W_res) + strip .base_layer... wait, actually for the normal path, collect_lora_params(base_sync_done=False) collects the base weights of the *actor's* base layers (W_res for PiSSA!) — exactly. And then replace_lora_wrapper converts the names to base_layer.* keys for the vllm patch loader.

Hmm wait, actually — why not just use the normal LoRA first-sync path for SVD-init too (i.e., delete the special SVD branch)? The normal path with base_sync_done=False collects base weights from the actor's base layers → W_res with plain names → replace_lora_wrapper → base_layer.* keys → model.load_weights → vLLM base = W_res. Then delta syncs work. That's the cleanest: the SVD branch is entirely redundant with the normal path, since the actor's base_layer weights ARE W_res.

Wait, but there's a subtlety: in the normal path, `collect_lora_params(module, layered_summon, base_sync_done=False)` with `layered_summon=False` uses `FSDP.summon_full_params` then iterates `peft_model.base_model.model.state_dict()` skipping "lora_" and "_flat_param" — collecting base weights (W_res). Then `replace_lora_wrapper` adds `.base_layer` back to the keys of target modules. Hmm wait — the state_dict keys of `peft_model.base_model.model` (the HF model inside PeftModel) for target modules are like `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.weight` (since the modules are lora-wrapped). The code strips `.base_layer` via replace, then `replace_lora_wrapper` re-adds it?? That seems odd... Let me re-read:

```python
name = name.replace("_fsdp_wrapped_module.", "").replace(".base_layer", "")
```

So `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.weight` → `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight`. Then in rollout_mode: `params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for ...}` → `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.base_layer.weight`. And then `convert_weight_keys(params, ...)` — let me check what that does. Then `model.load_weights(params)` with the patched qwen2 loader which resolves `base_layer` names via resolve_param_name. OK.

Why the strip-then-readd dance? Probably replace_lora_wrapper is a no-op for non-target modules and re-adds for target modules; the resolve_param_name in the patch tries plain name first, then base_layer variants. Whatever — the mechanics work.

So for the SVD-init first sync, the simplest correct fix is to **remove the special-case branch** (or make it collect the actor's actual base-layer weights = W_res). But careful: `_collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params` deliberately loads from disk via AutoModelForCausalLM... why? Maybe because of some FSDP state issue at first sync in async mode? Hmm. Note the comment in `_build_policy_model` around line 622-648: `if self._is_svd_init: ... low_cpu_mem_usage=not self._is_svd_init`. Let me read that section to understand the actor construction, to see if the actor's base weights might NOT be W_res (e.g., if the actor was loaded as residual base + adapter applied as PiSSA — peft's PiSSA init: when you load a peft model with init_lora_weights="pissa_niter_2" and an adapter... hmm, actually when loading a *saved* pissa adapter, peft just loads the A/B matrices; the residual base is already baked into residual_base/model.safetensors).

Wait, actually — hmm, important: what does the actor look like? `model.path=residual_base`, `lora_adapter_path=pissa_adapter`. So the actor = PeftModel(residual_base) with adapter loaded. base_layer = W_res, lora_B@lora_A = delta. Actor effective = W_res + delta = W_src. ✓.

Now let me also consider the `base_reference` health check: `base_reference_mae=0.0`, `base_reference_consistency=1.0` — that path (svd_init_adapter_ctx etc.) is fine.

And what about `training/rollout_probs_diff`? That's the standard instrumentation comparing actor log probs vs rollout log probs — KL ~3 → mismatch confirmed on the *training* rollouts, not just validation. And this mismatch existed from step 1.

Hold on, one more consideration: maybe the actual first sync (for the FIRST training rollout) was the initial one and validation used it, and the mismatch at step 1 arises differently. Let me check: in the observed metrics, step 1 has `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean=0.12` and `rollout_corr/kl=2.89`. If the first training rollout had used the correct initial sync (W_src), the step-1 KL would be ~0. It's 2.89, so the first training rollout already used the buggy double-delta weights. This means at least TWO syncs happened before the first training rollout (initial + one delta), consistent with val_before_train=True consuming the initial sync. Good.

Actually, wait — let me double-check by looking at the train.log for sync/debug messages and their order. Also check "base_sync_done" initialization: `self.base_sync_done: bool = "dummy" not in self.config.rollout.load_format` — load_format default is probably "safetensors" or "dummy_weights". If load_format were "dummy", base_sync_done would start True and the initial sync would never happen — but the debug dump shows `rollout_sync_initial` with base_sync_done_before=false, so it did happen. Good.

Now, let me also verify there isn't ANOTHER defect. The grad_norm=0: is that a defect? All rewards are 0 → GRPO advantage 0 → no gradient. Actually wait, is `actor/kl_loss=0` consistent with use_kl_loss=True? KL loss is computed vs ref log probs. With `use_kl_loss=True`, verl needs ref log probs — but there's no ref model (use_reference_policy?). Let me check: in GRPO with `algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False`, `actor.use_kl_loss=True`... the actor computes kl_loss vs `ref_log_prob` in the batch. Is `compute_ref_log_prob` called? In fit(), if `self.use_reference_policy` is False, ref_log_prob may not be computed → kl_loss = 0 or... hmm. In upstream verl, `kl_loss = -kl_coef * ...` — actually if use_kl_loss=True but no ref model, verl raises an error? Let me check the actor's update_policy code in this repo.

But hold on — is the zero-reward/zero-gradient situation itself "healthy" for this task? The task says the fixed experiment must preserve the bundle, data, budget, etc. The graded metric is "the final step-4 actor/rollout health metric". So the grader checks `val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae` (and agreement) — the fix should make actor == rollout → MAE ≈ 0, agreement ≈ 1. The reward being 0 everywhere is expected for a 0.5B model with 32-token responses (it can't solve GSM8K in 32 tokens), and advantages=0 → no weight updates → that's fine and arguably intended ("deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, response length 32"). The task says don't alter data/model/budget/metric logging — so I shouldn't try to make rewards nonzero. The health metric is the target.

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider whether advantages are truly zero because rewards are all-zero... GRPO computes advantage = (r - mean(r)) / std(r) per group; if all rewards equal (all 0), advantage = 0 (std=0 → division guarded). Yes → pg_loss=0 → grad_norm=0. Also entropy_coeff=0. So no learning happens at all. That's fine — the experiment is a "does the machinery work" test.

But wait — should I also check `actor/kl_loss: 0.0`? If use_kl_loss=True and ref_log_prob exists... The KL loss would be KL(actor || ref). Actor == ref initially (both W_src effective). But wait — the "ref" here: with `_is_lora`, `compute_ref_log_prob` → `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` → for SVD-init, `_svd_init_adapter_ctx` → uses frozen initial adapter → W_res + A_init B_init = W_src. So ref = pretrained. And actor = pretrained. KL loss = 0. ✓ consistent. And if the actor never updates, kl_loss stays 0. So `actor/kl_loss=0` is expected given no updates, not a bug. And `actor/grad_norm=0` is expected given zero advantages.

Hmm, but wait — actually is it? `actor/pg_loss=0.0` — pg_loss is `-(advantages * ratio).mean()` masked → 0 if advantages are 0. Yes.

Let me check if verl is installed in site-packages (pip freeze shows verl?). Actually PYTHONPATH=${VERL_ROOT} is used, so the workspace verl shadows any installed one. Let me try downloading the matching upstream commit... no network? Let me check.

Actually, a better approach: search the verl tree for the instrumentation (which is custom: `_write_rollout_policy_debug`, `log_final_policy_health`, `rollout_corr` etc.) — these are benchmark-added files. The defect is likely a subtle change in one of these custom or modified files. Let me list files that look custom/modified vs stock verl. - `_collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params` + SVD-init branch in rollout_mode (custom)

steps.reasoning_content:
No network. I'll rely on reasoning about the code itself. The design intent is documented in comments and debug dumps, and the health metric tells us the ground truth.

Let me now carefully trace the actual sync flow. Key questions:

1. When is `rollout_mode()` first called in async mode? (i.e., is there a sync before the val-before-train generation AND before the first train rollout?)
2. What weights does the vLLM engine hold after: (a) initial sync, (b) the "latest" delta sync?
3. What does the actor hold?

Also, importantly: is the divergence really "vLLM = W_pretrained + delta" (double delta)? Let me test this hypothesis numerically: compute forward log probs under (W_res + delta) vs (W_res + 2·delta) on some sample text and compare the per-token |Δ logprob| — check whether it matches the observed `rollout_corr/log_ppl_abs_diff` ≈ 2.9-3.2 and health MAE 2.256. If W_pretrained + delta vs W_res + delta differ by exactly delta, then log_ppl_abs_diff for the doubled-delta model... Let me compute.

    def update_policy(self, data: DataProto):
        # make sure we are in training mode
        self.actor_module.train()
        if not hasattr(self, "_debug_actor_update_policy_once"):
            self._debug_actor_update_policy_once = False
        if not self._debug_actor_update_policy_once and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0:
            _write_actor_policy_debug(
                "actor_update_policy",
                {
                    "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                    "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                    **_actor_adapter_state_payload(self.actor_module),
                },
            )
            self._debug_actor_update_policy_once = True

        temperature = data.meta_info["temperature"]  # temperature must be in the data.meta_info to avoid silent error

        select_keys = [
            "responses",
            "response_mask",
            "input_ids",
            "attention_mask",
            "position_ids",
            "old_log_probs",
            "advantages",
        ]
        if self.config.use_kl_loss:
            select_keys.append("ref_log_prob")
        safe_base_ref_log_prob = None
        if "base_ref_log_prob" in data.batch.keys():
            # TensorDict.select() corrupts this tensor in the current training path,
            # so carry a materialized copy across the selection boundary.
            safe_base_ref_log_prob = data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"].clone().contiguous()
        # Include pre-computed IS weights if present in batch
        # Weights are computed centrally in trainer and added to batch when algorithm.rollout_is=True
        if "rollout_is_weights" in data.batch.keys():
            select_keys.append("rollout_is_weights")
        # Include rollout_log_probs for computing rollout_corr metrics in bypass mode
        if "rollout_log_probs" in data.batch.keys():
            select_keys.append("rollout_log_probs")

        has_multi_modal_inputs = "multi_modal_inputs" in data.non_tensor_batch.keys()
        non_tensor_select_keys = ["multi_modal_inputs"] if has_multi_modal_inputs else []

        data = data.select(batch_keys=select_keys, non_tensor_batch_keys=non_tensor_select_keys)
        if safe_base_ref_log_prob is not None:
            data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"] = safe_base_ref_log_prob
        if (
            not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
            and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
            and "base_ref_log_prob" in data.batch.keys()
        ):
            _write_base_kl_debug(
                "actor_update_probe_after_select",
                {
                    "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                    "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                    **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                        "after_select",
                        data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"],
                        data.batch.get("old_log_probs"),
                    ),
                },
            )

        # Split to make minibatch iterator for updating the actor
        # See PPO paper for details. https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347
        mini_batches = data.split(self.config.ppo_mini_batch_size)

        on_policy = len(mini_batches) == 1 and self.config.ppo_epochs == 1

        metrics = {}
        for _ in range(self.config.ppo_epochs):
            for batch_idx, mini_batch in enumerate(mini_batches):
                if (
                    not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
                    and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
                    and "base_ref_log_prob" in mini_batch.batch.keys()
                ):
                    _write_base_kl_debug(
                        "actor_update_probe_mini_batch",
                        {
                            "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                            "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                            "mini_batch_idx": int(batch_idx),
                            **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                                "mini_batch_before_dynamic",
                                mini_batch.batch["base_ref_log_prob"],
                                mini_batch.batch.get("old_log_probs"),
                            ),
                        },
                    )
                if self.config.use_dynamic_bsz:
                    max_token_len = self.config.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu * self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
                    micro_batches, _ = prepare_dynamic_batch(mini_batch, max_token_len=max_token_len)
                else:
                    self.gradient_accumulation = (
                        self.config.ppo_mini_batch_size // self.config.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
                    )
                    micro_batches = mini_batch.split(self.config.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu)

                self.actor_optimizer.zero_grad()

                for micro_idx, micro_batch in enumerate(micro_batches):
                    if (
                        not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
                        and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
                        and "base_ref_log_prob" in micro_batch.batch.keys()
                    ):
                        _write_base_kl_debug(
                            "actor_update_probe_micro_before_to",
                            {
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                                "mini_batch_idx": int(batch_idx),
                                "micro_batch_idx": int(micro_idx),
                                **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                                    "micro_batch_before_to",
                                    micro_batch.batch["base_ref_log_prob"],
                                    micro_batch.batch.get("old_log_probs"),
                                ),
                            },
                        )
                    micro_batch = micro_batch.to(get_device_id())
                    micro_batch_metrics = {}
                    model_inputs = {**micro_batch.batch, **micro_batch.non_tensor_batch}
                    if (
                        not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
                        and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
                        and "base_ref_log_prob" in model_inputs
                    ):
                        _write_base_kl_debug(
                            "actor_update_probe_micro_after_to",
                            {
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                                "mini_batch_idx": int(batch_idx),
                                "micro_batch_idx": int(micro_idx),
                                **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                                    "micro_batch_after_to",
                                    model_inputs["base_ref_log_prob"],
                                    model_inputs.get("old_log_probs"),
                                ),
                            },
                        )
                        self._debug_base_ref_flow_once = True
                    response_mask = model_inputs["response_mask"]
                    old_log_prob = model_inputs["old_log_probs"]
                    advantages = model_inputs["advantages"]

                    entropy_coeff = self.config.entropy_coeff
                    loss_agg_mode = self.config.loss_agg_mode

                    calculate_entropy = self.config.calculate_entropy or (entropy_coeff != 0)

                    if self.config.use_dynamic_bsz:
                        loss_scale_factor = response_mask.shape[0] / self.config.ppo_mini_batch_size
                    else:
                        loss_scale_factor = 1 / self.gradient_accumulation

                    # all return: (bsz, response_length)
                    entropy, log_prob = self._forward_micro_batch(
                        model_inputs, temperature=temperature, calculate_entropy=calculate_entropy
                    )

                    rollout_old_log_prob = model_inputs["old_log_probs"]

                    loss_mode = self.config.policy_loss.get("loss_mode", "vanilla")
                    # vanilla -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_vanilla

                    # Extract pre-computed rollout correction weights if present
                    # Weights are computed centrally in trainer and added when algorithm.rollout_is=True
                    rollout_is_weights = model_inputs.get("rollout_is_weights", None)

                    # gpg -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_gpg
                    # clip_cov -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_clip_cov
                    policy_loss_fn = get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode)

                    # Compute policy loss (any function is expected to return 2 values)
                    pg_loss, pg_metrics = policy_loss_fn(
                        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
                        log_prob=log_prob,
                        advantages=advantages,
                        response_mask=response_mask,
                        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
                        config=self.config,
                        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
                    )
                    micro_batch_metrics.update(pg_metrics)

                    # Skip if using pure rollout correction mode (metrics already in pg_metrics)
                    rollout_log_prob = model_inputs.get("rollout_log_probs", None)
                    if loss_mode != "rollout_correction" and rollout_log_prob is not None:
                        # Compute metrics using CURRENT policy π_θ vs π_rollout
                        # Tracks evolving off-policy gap as π_θ updates during mini-batch training
                        from verl.trainer.ppo.rollout_corr_helper import compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs

                        rollout_corr_metrics = compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs(
                            log_prob=log_prob,
                            rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,
                            response_mask=response_mask,
                        )
                        micro_batch_metrics.update(rollout_corr_metrics)

                    policy_loss = pg_loss
                    if calculate_entropy and entropy is not None:

                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/entropy"] = entropy_agg.detach().item()
                        if entropy_coeff != 0:

                    if self.config.use_kl_loss:

        if "base_ref_log_prob" in data.batch.keys():
            # TensorDict.select() corrupts this tensor in the current training path,
            # so carry a materialized copy across the selection boundary.
            safe_base_ref_log_prob = data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"].clone().contiguous()
        # Include pre-computed IS weights if present in batch
        # Weights are computed centrally in trainer and added to batch when algorithm.rollout_is=True
        if "rollout_is_weights" in data.batch.keys():
            select_keys.append("rollout_is_weights")
        # Include rollout_log_probs for computing rollout_corr metrics in bypass mode
        if "rollout_log_probs" in data.batch.keys():
            select_keys.append("rollout_log_probs")

        has_multi_modal_inputs = "multi_modal_inputs" in data.non_tensor_batch.keys()
        non_tensor_select_keys = ["multi_modal_inputs"] if has_multi_modal_inputs else []

        data = data.select(batch_keys=select_keys, non_tensor_batch_keys=non_tensor_select_keys)
        if safe_base_ref_log_prob is not None:
            data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"] = safe_base_ref_log_prob
        if (
            not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
            and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
            and "base_ref_log_prob" in data.batch.keys()
        ):
            _write_base_kl_debug(
                "actor_update_probe_after_select",
                {
                    "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                    "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                    **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                        "after_select",
                        data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"],
                        data.batch.get("old_log_probs"),
                    ),
                },
            )

        # Split to make minibatch iterator for updating the actor
        # See PPO paper for details. https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347
        mini_batches = data.split(self.config.ppo_mini_batch_size)

        on_policy = len(mini_batches) == 1 and self.config.ppo_epochs == 1

        metrics = {}
        for _ in range(self.config.ppo_epochs):
            for batch_idx, mini_batch in enumerate(mini_batches):
                if (
                    not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
                    and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
                    and "base_ref_log_prob" in mini_batch.batch.keys()
                ):
                    _write_base_kl_debug(
                        "actor_update_probe_mini_batch",
                        {
                            "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                            "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                            "mini_batch_idx": int(batch_idx),
                            **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                                "mini_batch_before_dynamic",
                                mini_batch.batch["base_ref_log_prob"],
                                mini_batch.batch.get("old_log_probs"),
                            ),
                        },
                    )
                if self.config.use_dynamic_bsz:
                    max_token_len = self.config.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu * self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
                    micro_batches, _ = prepare_dynamic_batch(mini_batch, max_token_len=max_token_len)
                else:
                    self.gradient_accumulation = (
                        self.config.ppo_mini_batch_size // self.config.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
                    )
                    micro_batches = mini_batch.split(self.config.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu)

                self.actor_optimizer.zero_grad()

                for micro_idx, micro_batch in enumerate(micro_batches):
                    if (
                        not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
                        and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
                        and "base_ref_log_prob" in micro_batch.batch.keys()
                    ):
                        _write_base_kl_debug(
                            "actor_update_probe_micro_before_to",
                            {
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                                "mini_batch_idx": int(batch_idx),
                                "micro_batch_idx": int(micro_idx),
                                **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                                    "micro_batch_before_to",
                                    micro_batch.batch["base_ref_log_prob"],
                                    micro_batch.batch.get("old_log_probs"),
                                ),
                            },
                        )
                    micro_batch = micro_batch.to(get_device_id())
                    micro_batch_metrics = {}
                    model_inputs = {**micro_batch.batch, **micro_batch.non_tensor_batch}
                    if (
                        not self._debug_base_ref_flow_once
                        and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
                        and "base_ref_log_prob" in model_inputs
                    ):
                        _write_base_kl_debug(
                            "actor_update_probe_micro_after_to",
                            {
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                                "mini_batch_idx": int(batch_idx),
                                "micro_batch_idx": int(micro_idx),
                                **_base_ref_probe_payload(
                                    "micro_batch_after_to",
                                    model_inputs["base_ref_log_prob"],
                                    model_inputs.get("old_log_probs"),
                                ),
                            },
                        )
                        self._debug_base_ref_flow_once = True
                    response_mask = model_inputs["response_mask"]
                    old_log_prob = model_inputs["old_log_probs"]
                    advantages = model_inputs["advantages"]

                    entropy_coeff = self.config.entropy_coeff
                    loss_agg_mode = self.config.loss_agg_mode

                    calculate_entropy = self.config.calculate_entropy or (entropy_coeff != 0)

                    if self.config.use_dynamic_bsz:
                        loss_scale_factor = response_mask.shape[0] / self.config.ppo_mini_batch_size
                    else:
                        loss_scale_factor = 1 / self.gradient_accumulation

                    # all return: (bsz, response_length)
                    entropy, log_prob = self._forward_micro_batch(
                        model_inputs, temperature=temperature, calculate_entropy=calculate_entropy
                    )

                    # Keep rollout/eval-mode log probs for diagnostics such as base-model KL.
                    rollout_old_log_prob = model_inputs["old_log_probs"]
                    # for fully_async_policy recipe
                    if hasattr(self.config, "use_rollout_log_probs") and self.config.use_rollout_log_probs:
                        old_log_prob = rollout_old_log_prob
                    else:
                        if on_policy:
                            old_log_prob = log_prob.detach()
                        else:
                            old_log_prob = rollout_old_log_prob

                    loss_mode = self.config.policy_loss.get("loss_mode", "vanilla")
                    # vanilla -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_vanilla

                    # Extract pre-computed rollout correction weights if present
                    # Weights are computed centrally in trainer and added when algorithm.rollout_is=True
                    rollout_is_weights = model_inputs.get("rollout_is_weights", None)

                    # gpg -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_gpg
                    # clip_cov -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_clip_cov
                    policy_loss_fn = get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode)

                    # Compute policy loss (any function is expected to return 2 values)
                    pg_loss, pg_metrics = policy_loss_fn(
                        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
                        log_prob=log_prob,
                        advantages=advantages,
                        response_mask=response_mask,
                        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
                        config=self.config,
                        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
                    )
                    micro_batch_metrics.update(pg_metrics)

                    # Skip if using pure rollout correction mode (metrics already in pg_metrics)
                    rollout_log_prob = model_inputs.get("rollout_log_probs", None)
                    if loss_mode != "rollout_correction" and rollout_log_prob is not None:
                        # Compute metrics using CURRENT policy π_θ vs π_rollout
                        # Tracks evolving off-policy gap as π_θ updates during mini-batch training
                        from verl.trainer.ppo.rollout_corr_helper import compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs

                        rollout_corr_metrics = compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs(
                            log_prob=log_prob,
                            rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,
                            response_mask=response_mask,
                        )
                        micro_batch_metrics.update(rollout_corr_metrics)

                    policy_loss = pg_loss
                    if calculate_entropy and entropy is not None:
                        entropy_agg = agg_loss(loss_mat=entropy, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)
                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/entropy"] = entropy_agg.detach().item()
                        if entropy_coeff != 0:
                            policy_loss -= entropy_agg * entropy_coeff

                    if self.config.use_kl_loss:
                        ref_log_prob = model_inputs["ref_log_prob"]
                        # compute kl loss
                        kld = kl_penalty(
                            logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty=self.config.kl_loss_type
                        )
                        kl_loss = agg_loss(loss_mat=kld, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)

                        policy_loss = policy_loss + kl_loss * self.config.kl_loss_coef
                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/kl_loss"] = kl_loss.detach().item() * loss_scale_factor
                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/kl_coef"] = self.config.kl_loss_coef

                    if "base_ref_log_prob" in model_inputs:
                        base_ref_log_prob = model_inputs["base_ref_log_prob"]
                        # Compare rollout/eval-mode policy log probs against the frozen reference.
                        # This keeps base-model KL on the same inference-style footing as standard LoRA evals.
                        negative_approx_base_kl = torch.clamp(

                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/base_model_kl"] = base_model_kl.detach().item()
                        global_step = int(data.meta_info.get("global_steps", -1))
                        if not self._debug_base_kl_once and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0:

                            current_vs_base = log_prob.detach() - base_ref_log_prob
                            debug_payload = {
                                "stage": "actor_update",
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "global_step": global_step,
                                "rank": int(torch.distributed.get_rank()),
                                "mini_batch_idx": int(batch_idx),
                                "micro_batch_idx": int(micro_idx),
                                **_debug_base_kl_payload(rollout_old_log_prob, base_ref_log_prob, response_mask),
                                "current_log_prob_mean": float(log_prob.detach().mean().item()),
                                "rollout_vs_current_diff_mean": float(rollout_vs_current.mean().item()),
                                "rollout_vs_current_diff_abs_mean": float(rollout_vs_current.abs().mean().item()),
                                "current_vs_base_diff_mean": float(current_vs_base.mean().item()),
                                "current_vs_base_diff_abs_mean": float(current_vs_base.abs().mean().item()),
                            }
                            debug_path = _write_base_kl_debug("actor_update", debug_payload)
                            print(f"[DEBUG actor-update base KL] wrote {debug_path}")

                    if self.config.use_dynamic_bsz:
                        # relative to the dynamic bsz
                        loss = policy_loss * loss_scale_factor

In async mode, `wake_up()` → `rollout_mode()` (sync weights) and `sleep()` → `trainer_mode()`. The AgentLoopManager calls wake_up before each generation request and sleep after. So each generation (validation and training) is preceded by a weight sync (wake_up → rollout_mode). The FIRST wake_up does the initial sync; the SECOND wake_up does the delta sync.

Given val_before_train=True: the first generation = validation (val@0) → initial sync (W_src, no adapter) → vLLM = W_src = actor-at-init ✓ (correct!). Then step 1's training rollout → second wake_up → delta sync → add_lora(A_init,B_init) on top of W_src → vLLM = W_src + delta = W_res + 2·delta ✗ — diverged by delta. Every subsequent sync keeps the same double-delta state (remove_lora removes AB, add_lora adds AB again on W_src base).

Wait — but hold on: in async mode, is `generate_sequences` (the sync path at line ~1383, which calls rollout_mode per generation) used, or the AgentLoopManager's async path? The observed dumps show rollout_sync_initial and rollout_sync_latest, both written — consistent with at least 2 wake_ups.

Now let me verify: at step 1 the mismatch kl ≈ 2.89, and if val@0 was correct... hmm wait, actually — was the initial sync really "correct"? vLLM = W_src (from the disk load of source-qwen2.5-0.5b) and no adapter; actor = W_res + A_init B_init = W_src numerically (bf16 rounding aside). YES — correct at val@0.

Then, from the first delta sync onwards, everything is off by one delta_init. Health check at step 4: vLLM = W_src + A B vs actor = W_res + A B → differ by delta_init. MAE = 2.256.

Now — the fix. Given the machinery, the correct invariant is: **vLLM base weights must be the actor's base-layer weights (W_res)**, because the delta syncs add raw A·B on top. And since PiSSA's initial delta is non-zero, the adapter must be attached at the first sync too (otherwise val@0 would sample from W_res without the delta).

Approach: in `rollout_mode()`, replace the SVD-init initial-sync branch to:
1. Collect the actor's base-layer weights (W_res) — exactly like the normal LoRA initial path (`collect_lora_params(..., base_sync_done=False)` + `replace_lora_wrapper`).
2. Full-weights load into vLLM (peft_config=None, base_sync_done=False).
3. Then attach the current LoRA adapter: `update_weights(lora_params, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=True)` — the add_lora path.

Alternatively — simpler and equally correct: for the first sync, keep loading from disk but load the **residual base** (self.config.model.path) instead of the source model, then attach the adapter. But loading the actor's actual base-layer weights from the FSDP module is more robust (they're identical here: model.path IS the residual base dir, and the actor loads base weights from it unchanged).

    def _init_agent_loop_workers(self):
        self.agent_loop_workers = []
        num_workers = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers

        node_ids = [node["NodeID"] for node in ray.nodes() if node["Alive"] and node["Resources"].get("CPU", 0) > 0]
        for i in range(num_workers):
            # Round-robin scheduling over the all nodes
            node_id = node_ids[i % len(node_ids)]
            self.agent_loop_workers.append(
                self.agent_loop_workers_class.options(
                    name=f"agent_loop_worker_{i}",
                    scheduling_strategy=ray.util.scheduling_strategies.NodeAffinitySchedulingStrategy(
                        node_id=node_id, soft=True
                    ),
                ).remote(self.config, self.server_handles, self.reward_router_address)
            )

    def generate_sequences(self, prompts: DataProto) -> DataProto:
        """Split input batch and dispatch to agent loop workers.

        Args:
            prompts (DataProto): Input batch.

        Returns:
            DataProto: Output batch.
        """

        # Fix for Issue #4147: Always call wake_up() to ensure weight sync
        # The wake_up()/sleep() methods internally check free_cache_engine
        self.wake_up()
        if self.reward_model_manager:
            self.reward_model_manager.wake_up()

        chunkes = prompts.chunk(len(self.agent_loop_workers))
        outputs = ray.get(
            [
                worker.generate_sequences.remote(chunk)
                for worker, chunk in zip(self.agent_loop_workers, chunkes, strict=True)
            ]
        )
        output = DataProto.concat(outputs)
        # Fix for Issue #4147: Always call sleep() to ensure proper cleanup
        self.sleep()
        if self.reward_model_manager:
            self.reward_model_manager.sleep()

        # calculate performance metrics
        metrics = [output.meta_info.pop("metrics") for output in outputs]  # List[List[Dict[str, str]]]
        timing = self._performance_metrics(metrics, output)

        output.meta_info = {"timing": timing, **outputs[0].meta_info}
        return output

    def _performance_metrics(self, metrics: list[list[dict[str, str]]], output: DataProto) -> dict[str, float]:
        timing = {}
        t_generate_sequences = np.array([metric["generate_sequences"] for chunk in metrics for metric in chunk])
        t_tool_calls = np.array([metric["tool_calls"] for chunk in metrics for metric in chunk])
        timing["agent_loop/generate_sequences/min"] = t_generate_sequences.min()
        timing["agent_loop/generate_sequences/max"] = t_generate_sequences.max()
        timing["agent_loop/generate_sequences/mean"] = t_generate_sequences.mean()
        timing["agent_loop/tool_calls/min"] = t_tool_calls.min()
        timing["agent_loop/tool_calls/max"] = t_tool_calls.max()
